what_its_for: Fidaxomicin is an antibiotic used to treat a type of diarrhea and bowel infection caused by a germ called Clostridioides difficile (also called C. diff). It works by killing the C. diff bacteria in your intestines. It is only used for this specific type of infection and will not treat other infections like the common cold or flu.
how_to_take: Take fidaxomicin by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Take it exactly as your doctor tells you — do not skip doses or stop early, even if you start feeling better. Finishing the full course of treatment helps make sure all the harmful bacteria are gone and reduces the chance of the infection coming back.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one 200 mg tablet taken twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening), about 12 hours apart, for 10 days. Always follow the exact instructions from your doctor or pharmacist, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still several hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take the next one at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fidaxomicin tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container, away from excess heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid sharing this medication with anyone else, even if they have similar symptoms. Do not take extra doses or use it for longer than prescribed. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking any new prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some medicines may interact with fidaxomicin. Avoid unnecessary use of antibiotics, as this can lead to resistant bacteria.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; stomach pain that gets worse or does not improve; bloody or very watery diarrhea that worsens; fever; or any new or concerning symptoms during or after treatment. Also call if your diarrhea does not get better after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel some improvement in their diarrhea within a few days of starting fidaxomicin. However, it is very important to finish all 10 days of treatment even if you feel better, to fully clear the infection and prevent it from coming back. If you do not notice any improvement after 3 to 4 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine. The safety in pregnant or nursing women has not been fully established. This medication is approved for use in children as young as 6 months old in certain forms, but the dose will be different — always follow your child's doctor's instructions. If you have liver or kidney problems, let your doctor know, although dose adjustments are not usually needed.
